notes: Six items queued from the 2026-09-06 poll, all six read. The Registry's article bodies sit behind a subscription wall after the lede; where that is so, the headline and the visible lede are the whole evidentiary base and the locator says so.

coverage.note: Every Registry page carries the previous and next post titles and a related-articles rail, which is where nearly all of this feed's false address hits come from: 701 Main Street (Suisun City) and 2525 Park Blvd (Palo Alto) appeared in five of the six articles as furniture. Two articles were about buildings outside San Francisco — the SFO Superbay Hangar in San Mateo County and California Forever's Suisun City purchase — and one, on average new apartment size, named 321 Florida only in its own next-post link.

findings.description: DM Development refiled its plans for the shuttered Empire Theater in West Portal, enlarging the project to 172 apartments across 12 storeys with about 7,000 square feet of ground-floor retail, of which 26 units would be below market rate. The earlier filing was 64 units across nine storeys. The complex would rise on the theatre site and an adjacent property, currently occupied by a Super Cuts and a Goodwill, which would be demolished. The theatre closed early in the Covid-19 pandemic. The project is a proposal, so no name goes into the building block.

extra.site: the Empire Theater and an adjacent property
extra.former_use: Empire Theater, closed early in the Covid-19 pandemic

citation.label: The Registry, “DM Development Nearly Triples Empire Theater Redevelopment in San Francisco’s West Portal to 172 Units, 12 Stories,” 3 September 2026
citation.locator: headline and lede; the body is behind a subscription wall

raw.text: DM Development has refiled its plans for the shuttered Empire Theater in West Portal, expanding a pr[oject] …

findings.note: Corroborated by The San Francisco Standard, “A West Portal project doubled in size. It’s the latest in SF’s ‘F your feelings’ era,” 5 September 2026 (https://sfstandard.com/2026/09/05/west-portal-empire-theater-development-businesses/). The unit count, storey count, retail area, below-market count and the earlier 64-unit/nine-storey filing are taken from this second account, which is not paywalled. It is not a second entry — see the declined finding in news/items/sf-standard/2026-09-06.json.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 85 WEST PORTAL AVE → parcel 2979A019; sf-parcels has blklot 2979A019 active, 75–85 WEST PORTAL; the 2025 roll records it as commercial misc, built 1925. EAS puts 75, 79, 85 WEST PORTAL AVE on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 75.

publish.note: One event, one entry. /san-francisco/west-of-twin-peaks/west-portal-avenue/75/ already carries San Francisco YIMBY's 'Increased Plans For 85 West Portal Avenue, San Francisco' of 1 September 2026, which is the same enlarged filing reported two days earlier. The Registry's numbers and The Standard's are kept in this finding's extra and note, where they are the fuller record of the scheme, but the timeline carries one line for it.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 321 FLORIDA ST → parcel 3965022; sf-parcels has blklot 3965022 active, 309–321 FLORIDA; the 2025 roll records it as miscellaneous/mixed-use, built 1957. EAS puts 309, 321 FLORIDA ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 309.

publish.note: Put on the existing page /san-francisco/mission/florida-street/309/ — EAS puts 309 and 321 Florida Street on parcel 3965022, so the fact belongs on the page at the lower number. The page already carries San Francisco YIMBY's 'Permit Activity For 321 Florida Street' of 27 August 2026; this is kept as a separate entry because a construction start is a different milestone from a permit filing, not a second account of the same one. The card is on the homepage news grid.

findings.description: Sequoia Living and Heritage on the Marina filed a revised application enlarging their planned senior community to 120 units, on a site behind a Julia Morgan landmark. The visible lede states the revision would double the height of the earlier scheme. The project is a proposal and adds nothing to the building block; the Julia Morgan attribution is the outlet's characterisation of the existing landmark rather than a statement about a building this project would produce, and is recorded here only.

extra.change: revised application would double the height of the earlier scheme

findings.address_as_written: SFO Superbay Hangar; 701 Main Street, Suisun City; 2525 Park Blvd, Palo Alto
findings.description: Three Registry items about buildings outside San Francisco: a $132 million overhaul of the 421,000-square-foot Superbay Hangar at SFO, California Forever's purchase of 701 Main Street and two lots in Suisun City, and, in the related rail of both, a speculative office at 2525 Park Boulevard in Palo Alto.

citation.label: The Registry, three items of 4 September 2026

publish.note: Out of area. SFO is in San Mateo County; Suisun City and Palo Alto are not San Francisco. 701 Main Street matched only because the site covers a Main Street of its own — a false hit worth remembering, since it recurred in five of this feed's six articles as page furniture.

resolution.method: Not resolved: the finding is declined, so no parcel is sought.
